chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sin’ani (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qattan said: Musa ibn Ishaq narrated from Abu Ibrahim al-Tarjomani, from Salih ibn Bashir Abu Bashar al-Mari, who said: I heard al-Hasan narrating from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) narrated from his Lord, Glory be to His Majesty, that He said:

There are four characteristics: one is for Me, one is for you, one is between Me and you, and one is between you and My servants. As for the one that is for Me, it is that you worship Me and do not associate any partner with Me. As for the one that is for you, it is that whatever good you do, I will reward you for it. As for the one between Me and you, it is that from you is the supplication and upon Me is the response. As for the one between you and My servants, it is that you should be pleased for them what you are pleased for yourself. And Adam was not mentioned in this tradition.

key_terms.تَرْضَى لَهُمْ مَا تَرْضَى لِنَفْسِكَ: be pleased for them what you are pleased for yourself

ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics of the relationship between God and humanity according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this Hadith Qudsi addresses Adam directly, establishing a comprehensive covenant that defines the vertical relationship with God (monotheism and supplication) and the horizontal relationship with creation (ethical reciprocity). It serves as a foundational text in Shia theology for understanding the mutual rights between the Divine and humanity, emphasizing that divine justice ensures reward for deeds while requiring sincere devotion.
